items.title: Joe Darensbourg and Minor "Ram" Hall Interview, 1957-04-18
items.q: That's, it was comparable of, uh, Duke Ellington or Elvis Presley coming to Los Angeles.

ctx.x: Five or six hundred dollars. That's money, huh? Oh, easy. On one night. Oh, yeah. Easy. Cleaning up, huh? Easy, because you're going through the audience, uh, three or four times during the show. Uh-huh. Then, uh, we would have a little, uh, stash out there in the weeds, you know. Usually we played empty lots. I'd have me some bottles out there hid. When I sold all the doc's medicine, I'd get mine. Made a little extra money. Did Doc know about that? No, he didn't know. I should say not. We'd set that deal early.…

Play a little gig, huh? Yeah, we played the little towns, and believe it or not, I mean, uh, we, we, we, we, we, we, we were big shots when we hit those little towns. Yeah. That's, it was comparable of, uh, Duke Ellington or Elvis Presley coming to Los Angeles. Yeah.

It sounds fantastic now, but it's true. Yeah. They were all one to split. They wanted you to play. You, you, you, you, you was a big man when you hit one of those towns. Everybody wanted to see you. We played a little towns, like, uh, we played towns that guys had never heard a saxophone in person before. Never heard one. And the people in those little towns heard, heard much jazz before? No, no. Maybe once in a while. Some of the guys had left the town. We played towns that jazz had never come through, I mean…
